turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Please sit, I'll just take your vitals before Doctor calls you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya, sure. I'm twenty-four, usually fine with stairs, but I rushed from the metro and it's proper hot outside. I also have a standup at four, so I'm hoping this is quick.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Blood pressure is 118 over 76. Pulse 98. Oxygen saturation 98 percent. Temperature 36.8. Respiratory rate 18.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): 98 on the pulse, ha. I had a large cold coffee near the station, and one energy drink already this morning. The AC in here is a relief at least.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): You're done with me for now. Please wait, Doctor will call you.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come in. What is the problem today?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): My heart keeps racing and thumping, and I get breathless along with it. It started maybe three weeks back. My cousin's wedding shopping for Pune is also chaos, but that is a separate headache, not this one.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): When is it worse?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): At night, when I lie down, about four nights a week. Also right before my certification exam, or before a work meeting. If I sit still it settles in a few minutes. Mornings are mostly okay.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Wakes you from sleep?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Not exactly waking me. I'm already awake, scrolling, and then it starts. Sometimes the fan noise mixes with it, which is annoying.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest pain?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really. More a flutter than an actual pain.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fainting or blackout?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I don't fall or black out. I stay aware the whole time.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever, cough, or leg swelling?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, no cough, and my legs are normal. I had a sore throat last month, it cleared by itself, nothing now.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): How much coffee and energy drink in a day?

[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Coffee, three or sometimes four cups. On meeting days, two cans of Monster. My friend keeps scolding me about it, but I don't think the drinks are the problem. I'm not stressed, exams are just exams.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Cigarettes, no. I vape a mint pod, about ten to fifteen puffs a day. Started after college, so roughly two years now.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?

[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Hardly. A beer on some weekends, not every week. There is a new filter-coffee place downstairs in my building, you can smell the chicory from the lift, much better than beer.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicines you take?

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Only Crocin, the 650 one, when my head is paining, about once a week. Nothing else daily. My roommate offered me her white calming tablet last week, I did not take even one.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to medicines?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I know of. Crocin has always suited me.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thyroid, heart disease, or asthma, in you or the family?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't have any of those. My mother has thyroid, she takes a tablet for it, I forget the name. Father is fine. No heart attacks in the family, as far as I know.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you exercise? What is your work?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Software testing, a desk job, and a night shift now and then, which is why the late coffee happens. Gym, no. I only walk till the metro.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll listen to your chest. Breathe normally.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest is clear. Heart sounds are normal, no murmur. Pulse is regular just now, a little fast.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): So the heart is okay itself? At two in the morning it really does not feel okay. I even blamed my ceiling fan for a week, the ticking, I thought that was my pulse.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Listening alone cannot settle it. We will do an ECG, and thyroid blood tests.

[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): This night-time pattern, and the episodes before exams and meetings, with that much coffee, Monster and vaping, is most likely stimulant-related palpitations. I still have to exclude a rhythm problem and a thyroid issue.

[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright. But I'm really not a stressed person, doctor. The vape is only mint, it is not like a cigarette, and the Monster is just for the standup. Everyone on my team has one.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stop the energy drinks. Coffee, one cup a day. And stop the vape.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): One cup is quite strict. Can it be two, morning and a small one before the meeting?
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. One cup. Two is still too much while this is happening.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): When the thumping starts, do slow breathing. Breathe in for four counts, hold for four, out for six. Do that for five minutes, sitting.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): In for four, hold four, out for six. I'll try. My friend told me the same yoga thing last month and I laughed at her, so this is a bit embarrassing.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): ECG today, in the next room. Thyroid test is TSH and free T4, fasting is not needed. Lab is downstairs once the ECG is done.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Today itself is okay if the ECG is fast. Last time the lab queue, that was for my roommate, took nearly forty minutes. I might miss the four o'clock call.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): The ECG is about five minutes. Come back in one week with both reports.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): One week, noted. Do I stop the Crocin as well?
[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): No. Continue Crocin for the headache. Do not start that tablet from your roommate.
[SEG0048] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry, Doctor. ECG is free now. Shall I take him?
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes. ECG now, and book his review for one week.
[SEG0050] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Review is booked for one week. Come, we'll do the ECG.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Coming. If the reports come normal and the night thumping is still there, I still show up, yes? My mouth is dry from all this talking, is there water?
[SEG0052] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come in one week either way. If you faint, or the breathlessness gets much worse before that, go to emergency. Water is outside.

social_history.description: Three or sometimes four cups of coffee a day, and two cans of Monster energy drink on meeting days.
Does not smoke cigarettes. Vapes a mint pod, about 10 to 15 puffs a day, for roughly 2 years.
A beer on some weekends, not every week.
Software testing desk job, with a night shift now and then.
Does not go to the gym. Walks to the metro.

clinical_assessment.assessment: Most likely stimulant-related palpitations from coffee, energy drinks and vaping
clinical_assessment.basis: Night-time episodes and episodes before exams and meetings, with heavy coffee, Monster and vaping
Doctor says a rhythm problem still has to be excluded
Doctor says a thyroid issue still has to be excluded

procedures_and_investigations.name: TSH and free T4
procedures_and_investigations.indication: exclude a thyroid cause of palpitations

clinical_actions.description: ECG today in the next room
Thyroid blood tests, TSH and free T4, fasting not required, at the lab downstairs after the ECG
Stop energy drinks, limit coffee to one cup a day, and stop vaping.
When thumping starts, sit and breathe in for four counts, hold for four, and breathe out for six, for five minutes.
Continue Crocin for headache and do not start the roommate's calming tablet.
Go to emergency if you faint or if the breathlessness gets much worse.
Follow-up consultation

No family heart attacks was hedged with 'as far as I know' and was not recorded as a firm negative.

spec.situation: Young adult with palpitations and breathlessness, worse at night and before exams or work meetings; downplays stress, drinks a lot of coffee and energy drinks, vapes; friend or partner contributes. Doctor orders ECG and thyroid tests, discusses breathing exercises.
features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.

omissions.text: Chest pain history was recorded inaccurately: patient did not clearly deny chest pain; they said 'Sometimes, not really. More a flutter than an actual pain,' indicating equivocal/minimal chest discomfort rather than a definite negative.

omissions.text: Patient denied cigarette smoking specifically ('Cigarettes, no'). This is not the same as denying all smoking because the patient does vape.
Patient said chest pain was not really present; it was 'more a flutter than an actual pain.' The recorded chest discomfort as present overstates this symptom.
Doctor advised follow-up in one week regardless of whether the ECG/lab reports are normal and symptoms persist ('Come in one week either way').
